subject: Cross-border legal basis checklist for DPA — Stellar Health
messages:
From: Caroline Turner <caroline.turner@stellarhealth.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Legal Ops <legal.ops@stellarhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cross-border legal basis and Art.30 ledger — initial checklist request

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the DPA draft. As part of our internal review ahead of procurement sign-off, our privacy team asked for two things from Redwood to confirm our cross-border controls:

1) A short checklist confirming the legal basis you rely on for transfers out of the EU (Standard Contractual Clauses, adequacy, or other mechanisms) and which subprocessors are involved in any transfers.
2) A populated Art. 30-style ledger (we've attached a small template) showing categories of personal data you process for Stellar Health, retention periods, and subprocessors handling those categories.

Could you let us know timeline and whether you can provide the completed CSV and a short narrative for our DPIA reviewers? If you prefer, we can take a working session next week to walk through details.

Thanks,
Caroline Turner
Privacy Program Manager
Stellar Health

Attachments: Art30_Ledger_Template.csv (template)
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
To: Caroline Turner <caroline.turner@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-21T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border legal basis and Art.30 ledger — initial checklist request

Hi Caroline — thanks for the clear ask and the template. We're happy to provide both items. Quick proposed plan: 

- We will complete the Art.30 CSV with the data categories for the Stellar Health integration and mark which subprocessors may access each category (target: 3 business days).
- We'll provide a 1-page narrative that states our transfer mechanisms (SCCs + supplementary technical measures) and references the DPA appendix where we map subprocessors to regions (target: 2 business days).
- If you want a walkthrough, I can set up a 30-minute call after we share the files.

I've looped in Kim (Legal Ops handoff) and Laura (Privacy compliance) to review the ledger and the narrative before we send it to you.

Deliverables: completed Art.30 ledger (CSV), DPA transfer narrative (PDF), list of subprocessors with region tags (XLSX).

Do these timelines work for you?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Partnerships 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-22T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border legal basis and Art.30 ledger — internal review notes

Rafael / Laura — quick internal notes before we finalize: 

- Use SCCs as primary transfer mechanism for any EEA→US subprocessors; include reference to the latest EDPB guidance in the narrative.
- Call out our encryption-in-flight and at-rest controls as "supplementary technical measures" (brief bullets are fine).
- For the ledger: ensure we list the data categories at a reasonably granular level (e.g., "user identifiers, messages/content, metadata, service logs") and map retention to each category.
- Subprocessors: include our logging/storage vendor and the US-based inference cluster (dedicated vpc) — mark those as potential cross-border recipients.

I'll do a pass on the CSV tonight and push a draft to the Drive link Rafael shared. Laura, can you confirm retention periods for analytics logs?

Kim
Lead, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Caroline Turner <caroline.turner@stellarhealth.com>, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-26T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border legal basis and Art.30 ledger — final delivery

Hi Caroline,

Thanks for your patience — attached are the completed artifacts for Stellar Health:

- Art30_Ledger_StellarHealth.csv (populated per your template)
- DPA_Transfer_Narrative_StellarHealth.pdf (one-page summary of legal basis and measures)
- Subprocessor_Matrix_Regions.xlsx (list of subprocessors with region tags and whether SCCs apply)

Summary (short): we rely on SCCs for transfers from the EEA to the US for the subprocessors listed in the matrix; for transfers to adequacy countries we rely on recognized adequacy decisions. We have applied encryption-in-flight, limited access controls, and contractually enforced processor obligations as supplementary measures.

Next steps if useful: 1) we can join your DPIA working session to run through any outstanding questions, 2) confirm if Stellar wants the ledger ingested into your compliance portal or if a CSV is sufficient.

Attachments: Art30_Ledger_StellarHealth.csv, DPA_Transfer_Narrative_StellarHealth.pdf, Subprocessor_Matrix_Regions.xlsx

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
